evidenceAudit.scope: Respiratory distress in newborns in India: recognition, Silverman-Anderson scoring, oxygen targets, CPAP thresholds by gestation, surfactant for respiratory distress syndrome (RDS), feeding and fluids, and ventilation and referral criteria, built on the ICMR Respiratory Distress in Neonates STW (July 2020).
findings: Definition (respiratory rate above 60/min, chest retractions, nasal flaring, grunting or cyanosis; SpO2 below 91%), causes, Silverman-Anderson score thresholds, oxygen by nasal prongs 0.5–1 L/min (maximum 2), SpO2 target 91–95%, CPAP indications by gestation, severe distress (SAS 5 or more or FiO2 above 60–70%), avoidance of routine blood tests and X-rays, feeding rules and ventilation and referral criteria checked against the ICMR STW (July 2020).
Poractant alfa dose (2.5 mL/kg, then up to two 1.25 mL/kg doses 12 hours apart) from the Curosurf US label.
unverifiedSections: The ICMR workflow says surfactant 'as per indication' without a dose or product; the poractant dose is from its US label.
Extracted SAS thresholds were printed ambiguously ('SAS 4 >'); read as 4 or more; confirm against the printed workflow.
CPAP pressure and FiO2 settings are not in the workflow.
Causes other than RDS and pneumonia (transient tachypnoea, meconium aspiration, congenital heart disease) are general knowledge.
Drug cautions, contraindications and renal or hepatic adjustment lines without a source tag are general pharmacology statements and need formulary confirmation.

pathophysiology.summary: Respiratory distress is one of the commonest reasons for newborn admission in India. In preterm babies the usual cause is respiratory distress syndrome (RDS) from surfactant deficiency, which collapses alveoli and causes grunting, retractions and hypoxaemia; in term babies, pneumonia or sepsis, transient tachypnoea and meconium aspiration are common. The ICMR workflow grades severity with the Silverman-Anderson score (SAS), gives oxygen to keep SpO2 between 91% and 95% (higher levels risk retinopathy of prematurity), starts continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) early, especially below 32 weeks, and refers for ventilation when distress is severe or CPAP fails.
keyMechanisms: Surfactant deficiency raises alveolar surface tension, so alveoli collapse at end-expiration (RDS).
Collapse reduces lung compliance and causes hypoxaemia and increased work of breathing.
Grunting is the baby's own PEEP against a partly closed glottis.
CPAP and surfactant keep alveoli open.

physicalSigns: Lower chest retractions, nasal flaring, grunting (ICMR STW)
Prolonged capillary filling time in shock
redFlags: SAS 5 or more or FiO2 above 60–70%: severe; ventilate or refer (ICMR STW)
precipitants: Maternal fever, prolonged rupture of membranes (sepsis)

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Preterm, onset at birth, ground-glass lungs.
Maternal risk factors, temperature instability; see Neonatal sepsis topic.
Term, after caesarean, improves within 24–48 hours.
Cyanosis out of proportion to distress; murmur; poor response to oxygen.

SpO2 below 91% or any distress (SAS 1–3); early CPAP if SAS 3 or more.
SAS 5 or more or FiO2 above 60–70%.

clinicalManagement.title: Assess
actions: Score SAS; measure SpO2, respiratory rate and CFT (ICMR STW).
Avoid unnecessary CBC, CRP and routine ABG (ICMR STW).

clinicalManagement.title: Oxygen
actions: Nasal prongs 0.5–1.0 L/min, maximum 2 L/min; target SpO2 91–95% (ICMR STW).

clinicalManagement.title: CPAP
actions: 32 weeks or more: CPAP if SAS 4 or more or no improvement on oxygen (ICMR STW).
Below 32 weeks: CPAP if SpO2 below 91% or any distress; early CPAP if SAS 3 or more (ICMR STW).

clinicalManagement.title: Feeds and fluids
actions: Breastfeed if respiratory rate below 70/min and not on support; otherwise orogastric feeds (ICMR STW).
IV fluids only for severe distress or contraindication to enteral feeds (ICMR STW).

clinicalManagement.title: Ventilate or refer
actions: Severe distress (SAS 5 or more or FiO2 above 60–70%), CPAP failure, shock or repeated apnoea: ventilate or refer with the transport workflow (ICMR STW).
Pneumonia or sepsis: treat per unit protocol and the neonatal sepsis workflow (ICMR STW).

regimens.dose: 0.5–1.0 L/min, maximum 2 L/min, titrated to SpO2 91–95%
regimens.duration: Until SpO2 above 95% on air or support escalated
adjustments: Paediatric: This is a neonatal topic; doses are for newborns.
Penicillin allergy: Not an antibiotic; penicillin allergy does not change this medicine.

regimens.dose: Initial 2.5 mL/kg (200 mg/kg); then up to two doses of 1.25 mL/kg (100 mg/kg) about 12 hours apart if RDS persists; maximum total 5 mL/kg
adjustments: Paediatric: This is a neonatal topic; doses are for newborns.
Penicillin allergy: Not an antibiotic; penicillin allergy does not change this medicine.
ICMR STW: consider surfactant for RDS 'as per indication' (no dose).
monitoring: Heart rate, SpO2 and BP during dosing (bradycardia, desaturation)
Adjust oxygen and ventilation after dosing
contraindications: Only by clinicians experienced in neonatal intubation
No suction for 1 hour after dosing unless obstruction

medicationPlan.note: Oxygen, CPAP and referral thresholds are from the ICMR Respiratory Distress in Neonates STW (July 2020); surfactant dose from the Curosurf label. India-only topic; the Saudi topic is unchanged. Not clinically reviewed.

teaching.scope: Newborn respiratory distress in Indian units.
learningObjectives: Start CPAP early and know when to refer.
keyPoints: Respiratory rate above 60, retractions, grunting or cyanosis = distress.
SAS 5 or more or FiO2 above 60–70%: ventilate or refer.
pitfalls: Routine blood tests and X-rays in every baby.
Unnecessary IV fluids instead of feeds.
